correctness_confidence.basis: Hand-checked: Thm 1 chain (Lemma 15, Prop 8 normalisation, weakening to 2^(-6M-4) n^(-2M-1)); Lemmas 6-7; Prop 8 and the explicit Thm 3 instance (a/r tends to 16, exponent -3C/4+(2+t)log17/C); Cor 10-11, Cor 16; Thm 5 lower bound (Mathieu route) and Prop 18. Exact rational computation: Thm 5 upper family gives rho^2 = 0.12597 at m=100, k=0 (limit 1/8). Thm 4/13 checked only structurally.

rigor.basis: Explicit constants in Thm 1, Prop 8, Thm 3 (n >= 10^4 instance), Prop 18 and Lemmas 6-7. Thm 4 and Thm 13 rest on existential steps: Lemma 12 weights are stated to be existential and possibly large, the implicit-function step in Thm 4 has unquantified constants, and the O(eps^2) error bookkeeping is summarised rather than shown. The 34-class check is by an AI tool the paper itself says is not independent.

novelty.basis: The sharp circle-only constant 1/sqrt(8) (Thm 5) and the characterisation b_n tends to infinity (Thm 2) look new relative to the cited work [1]-[4]. Thm 3 removes the log n factor of [1]. The negative answer to Erdos 973 is credited to [2], and Cor 10 only refines it. The literature could not be checked (no web), so the comparison rests on the paper's own account.

significance.basis: Niche question about polynomial differentiation residuals. The main quantitative question for one interior zero (exponent between 13/6 and 1/6) is left open, and the superalgebraic family has no explicit rates or constants. Useful for the interior-zero threshold; limited beyond it.

reproducibility.basis: No code or data files. The Thm 5 family is explicit and I reproduced it exactly. The K=3 instance and the 40- and 60-digit checks are given without per-n tables, and the closing numerical report conflicts with a trivial bound (see objections). The authors' own consistency checks are not independent.

summary: The paper gives an interior-zero criterion for polynomial differentiation residuals with explicit finite-degree bounds (Thm 1, Prop 8, Thm 3); a sharp circle-only constant 1/sqrt(8) (Thm 5, with the upper family confirmed numerically); a superalgebraic construction with M_A interior zeros (Thm 4); a one-zero family with residual asymptotic to sqrt(15)/4^(4/3) n^(-1/6) (Prop 14); and an explicit n^(-13/6) lower bound for exactly one interior zero (Prop 18). Most of the proof chains check out on reading. The explicit K=3 numerical report conflicts with a trivial bound, and the Thm 4 and Thm 13 constructions are only sketched at the error-bookkeeping level. Major revision is needed before the claims can be relied on.
strengths: Thm 1 gives an explicit lower bound for any complex slope when the polynomial has M interior zeros; the arithmetic down to 2^(-6M-4) n^(-2M-1) checks.
Prop 8 is a clean finite certificate, and Lemmas 6-7 (normalisation, the ODE identity, Cauchy estimates for the moments) are correct as far as I checked.
Thm 5: the lower bound via the Mathieu variational route gives inf over lambda of g_n tending to 1/8, and the explicit upper family gives rho^2 tending to 1/8 (0.12597 at n=600).
Prop 18 gives an explicit n^(-13/6) lower bound for exactly one interior zero, consistent with the moment bookkeeping of Lemma 6.2 and Prop 8.

The disclosures are candid: AI-assisted checks are flagged as non-independent, existence-only statements are labelled as such, optimality is declared open, and the prior answer to Erdos 973 is credited.
weaknesses: The superalgebraic result (Thm 4) and the one-zero construction (Thm 13) are existence arguments: no explicit M_A, C_A or N_A, and the Lemma 12 weights are non-explicit.
The error terms in the Thm 4 implicit-function step (O(eps^2), analytic dependence of Phi, moment targets for j >= 4 at eps = 0) are asserted in a few lines and not shown.
The numerical section is not reproducible as written: no per-n table, no statement of which n produces which value, and no code.
The gap between exponents 13/6 and 1/6 for one interior zero is left open, as the paper acknowledges.
The comparisons depend heavily on [1] and [2], which could not be checked here.
potential_errors: Section 9, K=3 instance: the reported n^(1/6) rho(P_n) of about 282,244,238 for n = 10^5 to 10^7 implies rho of about 4.1x10^7 at n = 10^5. For any polynomial with P(0)=1 and zeros in the closed disk, rho <= n + |P'(0)| <= (2+o(1)) n when the zeros are on or near the circle, as here. So the value cannot be the residual at n = 10^5 or 10^6. The n is not stated.
strong_novelty_candidates: Sharp circle-only constant 1/sqrt(8) for s-circle_n and r-circle_n (Thm 5), with a Mathieu-type lower bound and an explicit Gaussian upper family.
Characterisation of superalgebraic budgets by b_n tending to infinity (Thm 2), combining the finite-budget bound of Thm 1 with the construction of Thm 4.
Explicit one-interior-zero lower bound n^(-13/6) with explicit constants (Prop 18).
unresolved_material_objections: Numerical support for the K=3 instance of Thm 4 (Section 9, final paragraph): the stated value is incompatible with the trivial bound rho <= n + |P'(0)| at n = 10^5 and 10^6, and the paper does not say which n the value refers to. Either the value is misreported or the instance is not the stated construction. To resolve: a per-n table of rho, P'(0) and the zero locations for the instance, with the 60-digit parameters. Until then the explicit K=3 instance is unverified. The asymptotic theorems are not disproved by this.
